class.name: Warden (LotR)
class.proficiency: Strength, Wisdom, Animal Handling, Athletics, Survival, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception

trait.name: Warden
trait.text:
"Travelers scowl at us, and countrymen give us scornful names."
In this age of the world, when shadows grow deeper with every passing year, you have sworn to defend all who cannot defend themselves. Often, your choice forces you to forsake civilized areas, to better guard their inhabitants from what lurks right outside their fences. This has made you a stranger in the eyes of the common folk, a threatening figure like those you are protecting them from.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 60

feature.name: Starting Warden
feature.text:
As a 1st-level Warden, you begin play with 10 + your Constitution modifier hit points.
You are proficient with the following items, in addition to any proficiencies provided by your race or background.
• Armor: light armor, medium armor, shields • Weapons: simple weapons, martial weapons • Tools: none • Skills: Choose 3 from Animal Handling, Athletics, Explore, Hunting, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception, and Travel
You begin play with the following equipment, in addition to any equipment provided by your background.
• (a) hide armor or (b) leather shirt • (a) a martial weapon and a shield or (b) a martial melee weapon and a simple melee weapon • (a) a great bow and a quiver of 20 arrows or (b) two simple melee weapons
If you forgo this starting equipment, as well as the items offered by your background, you start with 5d4 × 10 gp to buy your equipment.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 60

feature.name: Multiclass Warden
feature.text:
If your group uses the optional rule on multiclassing in the Player's Handbook, here's what you need to know if you choose warden as one of your classes.
Ability Score Minimum: As a multiclass character, you must have at least the following ability score(s) to take a level in this class, or to take a level in another class if you are already a warden.
• Wisdom 13
Proficiencies Gained: When you gain your first level in a class other than your initial class, you gain only some of your new class's starting proficiencies, here are the proficiencies you gain when you take your first level as a warden.
• Armor: light armor, medium armor, shields • Weapons: simple weapons, martial weapons
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 60

feature.name: Shadow Path
feature.text:
Path of Despair: Self-doubt is often the way that the Shadow chooses to reach the heart of those who oppose it. For they know that the Enemy is strong and terrible and that those they protect are too naive or weak to fend for themselves. Every day they ask themselves: will my strength be enough to prevail, or will I drag down the innocent in defeat?
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 61

feature.name: Shadow-Lore
feature.text:
Beginning at 1st level, you have significant experience studying, tracking, and hunting the servants of the Shadow. Choose a kind of favored foe: Beasts, Evil Men, Giants, Monstrosities, Orcs, or Undead. You can add your Wisdom modifier to the damage roll whenever you hit one of your favored foes, as well as to saving throws you make against their special abilities. Additionally, you have advantage on Wisdom (Hunting) checks to track your favored foes, as well as on Intelligence checks to recall information about them. You also learn one language of your choice that is spoken by your favored foes, if they speak one at all. You choose one additional favored foe at 6th level, and again at 10th level. As you gain levels, your choices should reflect the types of enemies you have encountered on your adventures.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 61

feature.name: Warded Lands
feature.text:
You are particularly familiar with the lands you have sworn to protect and are adept at travelling and surviving in such regions. Choose two warded lands from among the following: Arthedain, Cardolan, Enedwaith, Eregion, Lindon, and Rhudaur (the Loremaster may wish to expand or alter this list depending on the chosen setting). When you make an Intelligence or Wisdom check related to your warded lands, your proficiency bonus is doubled if you are using a skill that you're proficient in. During journeys in your warded lands, you gain the following benefits:
• You are allowed to cover more than one role without penalties. Remember that the same role cannot be assigned to more than one Player-hero, unless there are more than four Company members (see page 101).
• You have advantage on fatigue saving throws at the end of journeys that start and end in your warded lands.
• Double your speed for the purpose of calculating your travel pace within your warded lands. While tracking other creatures, you also learn their exact number, their sizes, and how long ago they passed through the area.
Finally, a Company including a Warden that spends a Fellowship Phase in a warded land can choose the Gather Rumors undertaking as a free undertaking (see page 112). You choose two additional warded lands at 6th level, and again at 10th level. As you gain levels, your choices should reflect the regions you have visited on your adventures.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 61

feature.name: Fighting Style
feature.text:
At 2nd level, you adopt a particular style of fighting as your speciality. Choose one of the following options. You cannot take a Fighting Style option more than once, even if you later get to choose again.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 61

feature.name: Fighting Style: Archery
feature.text:
You gain a +2 bonus to attack rolls you make with ranged weapons.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 61

feature.name: Fighting Style: Duelling
feature.text:
When you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and no other weapons, you gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls with that weapon.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 61

feature.name: Fighting Style: Protection
feature.text:
When a creature you can see hits you or a target other than you that is within 5 feet of you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to the target's AC for that attack, potentially causing the attack to miss. You must be wielding a shield or a finesse weapon.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 61

feature.name: Fighting Style: Two-Weapon Fighting
feature.text:
When you engage in two-weapon fighting, you can add your ability modifier to the damage of the second attack.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 61

feature.name: Virtue
feature.text:
Also at 2nd level, and again at 4th, 6th, 8th, and 10th level, you can take a common or cultural virtue of your choice. You can take each virtue only once. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. At 2nd, 6th, and 10th level, instead of taking a virtue you can gain a craft slot and a craft of your choice from the Scholar's Crafts list (see page 64).
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 61

feature.name: Warden Oath
feature.text:
Wardens are not soldiers sworn into service to a lord, but obey personal oaths they would never think of breaking, whether they choose to be Forayers or Hunters.
At 3rd level, you swear your oath as a Warden. You might choose to be a Forayer or a Hunter, both detailed at the end of the calling description. Your choice grants you features at 3rd level and again at 7th level.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 61

feature.name: Rumour of the Earth
feature.text:
Beginning at 3rd level, you can use your action to focus your awareness on the region around you. You can sense whether and which of your favored foes are present within a number of miles of you equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1; double this value if you are in your warded lands). This feature doesn't reveal the creatures' location or number. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 62

feature.name: Virtue Improvement
feature.text:
Also at 4th level, you can take a common or cultural virtue of your choice. You can take each virtue only once. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 61

feature.name: Extra Attack
feature.text:
When you reach 5th level you make two attacks when you take the Attack action on your turn, instead of one.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 62

feature.name: Virtue Improvement
feature.text:
Also at 6th level, you can take a common or cultural virtue of your choice. You can take each virtue only once. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. At 6th level, instead of taking a virtue you can gain a craft slot and a craft of your choice from the Scholar's Crafts list (see page 64).
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 61

feature.name: Virtue Improvement
feature.text:
Also at 8th level, you can take a common or cultural virtue of your choice. You can take each virtue only once. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 61

feature.name: Long Stride
feature.text:
Starting at 9th level, you can use the Dash action as a bonus action on your turn. Also, if you are in one of your warded lands, moving through difficult terrain costs you no extra movement.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 62

feature.name: Virtue Improvement
feature.text:
Also at 10th level, you can take a common or cultural virtue of your choice. You can take each virtue only once. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. At 10th level, instead of taking a virtue you can gain a craft slot and a craft of your choice from the Scholar's Crafts list (see page 64).
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 61

feature.name: Warden Oath: Forayer
feature.text:
From such men the Lord Denethor chose his forayers, who crossed the Anduin secretly (how or where, they would not say) to harry the Orcs and other enemies that roamed between the Ephel Duath and the River.
You patrol the land ceaselessly seeking to ambush the servants of the Enemy, for they are found in many places, not in Mordor only.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 62

feature.name: Bonus Proficiency (Forayer)
feature.text:
When you choose this oath at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Stealth skill. If you are already proficient, or if you are in one of your warded lands, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 62

feature.name: Ambusher (Forayer)
feature.text:
Starting at 3rd level, you excel at ambushing your enemies. You can add your Wisdom modifier to your initiative rolls, and you have advantage on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn. In addition, you gain the Sneak Attack feature (see page 58). The extra damage is 1d6, and it increases to 2d6 when you reach 9th level in this calling.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 62

feature.name: Harrier (Forayer)
feature.text:
Starting at 7th level, you can use the Hide action as a bonus action on your turn.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 62

feature.name: Warden Oath: Hunter
feature.text:
"I am called Strider," answered Aragorn. "I came out of the North. I am hunting Orcs."
You have chosen to prey upon the enemies of the Free Peoples, as a hunter relentlessly seeks a dangerous quarry.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 62

feature.name: Bonus Proficiency (Hunter)
feature.text:
When you choose this oath at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the Hunting skill. If you are already proficient, or when tracking your favored foes, you add double your proficiency bonus to checks you make with it.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 62

feature.name: Hunter's Prey (Hunter)
feature.text:
At 3rd level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 62

feature.name: Hunter's Prey: Foe-Hammer (Hunter)
feature.text:
Your tenacity can wear down the most potent foes. When you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can roll one additional weapon damage die on the damage roll if it's below its hit points maximum. You can deal this extra damage only once per turn.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 62

feature.name: Hunter's Prey: Goblin-Cleaver (Hunter)
feature.text:
Once on each of your turns when you make a weapon attack, you can make another attack with the same weapon against a different creature that is within 5 feet of the original target and within range of your weapon.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 63

feature.name: Hunter's Prey: Troll-Killer (Hunter)
feature.text:
Once on each of your turns when you make a weapon attack against a Large or larger creature, you can make another attack with the same weapon against the same creature.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 63

feature.name: Defensive Tactics (Hunter)
feature.text:
At 7th level, you gain one of the following features of your choice.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 63

feature.name: Defensive Tactics: Multiattack Defence (Hunter)
feature.text:
When a creature hits or misses you with an attack, you add your proficiency bonus to your AC against all subsequent attacks made by that creature for the rest of the turn.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 63

feature.name: Defensive Tactics: Stout Resistance (Hunter)
feature.text:
You gain proficiency in a saving throw of your choice.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 63

feature.name: Defensive Tactics: Swift to Fly (Hunter)
feature.text:
You can use the Disengage action as a bonus action on your turn.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 63
